title: The Soccer-to-Rugby Swap
takeaway: On a prompt asking the model to think of an item and then name it, the J-lens readout at the position just before the answer already contains the answer, and exchanging that lens content — Soccer out, Rugby in — makes the model report the swapped concept instead. The verbal report follows the contents of the workspace at the time of reporting, causally and not just correlationally.
walkthrough:
In the article this is a live widget, not a static image. It is the paper's first test of [[verbal-report]], the first of the five workspace properties: a worked example on the left, run once without and once with an intervention, and two aggregate panels on the right. Hovering a dot in either right-hand panel shows the trial behind it, including its prompt and its top lens tokens.

The example is the [[think-of-a-category-task]], run on Sonnet 4.5 of the [[claude-model-family]]. The prompt reads "Think of a sport. Answer in one word.", and the [[jacobian-lens]] is read at the colon after "Assistant" — the last position before the answer appears. Under the "Original" label sit two ranked bar lists for that position. The orange list is the [[j-lens-readout]] at L92; layers are numbered as percentages of depth ([[layer-percentage-indexing]]), and L92 is the final layer of the workspace range ([[workspace-layers]]). The grey list is the model's actual next-token logits. Both lists put Soccer first, at log-probability $-0.32$ in the lens and $-0.03$ in the logits, and the model answers "Soccer".

The block labeled with the swap repeats both readouts after a [[lens-coordinate-swap]]. At every token position, the activation's projection onto the Soccer [[j-lens-vector]] is subtracted and an equal-magnitude projection onto the Rugby vector is added; nothing else changes, and the forward pass continues. Rugby now leads both lists — $-0.23$ in the lens, $-0.00$ in the logits — and the model reports "Rugby" as the sport it thought of.

The top-right panel scales up the correlational half. For ten candidate answers in each of fourteen categories, it plots the [[spearman-correlation]] between the candidates' ordering in the lens readout and their ordering in the output logits, at three workspace layers. Bars are medians across categories; each dot is one category. The median rises from about 0.42 at L54 to 0.73 at L75 and 0.86 at L92. Agreement tightens as the readout layer approaches the point of speaking.

The bottom-right panel scales up the causal half. Each line is one swap trial: a target drawn at random from the category, restricted to targets that began at output rank 11 or worse, so the swap cannot merely amplify an answer already in contention. The rank axis is logarithmic, running from 1 to 1k+, with rank 1 at the top. Across the 67 trials shown, the median target rank moves from 36 before the swap to 3 after it, and no target ends worse than rank 10. The section adds that swaps along pure J-lens vectors put the target into the top-5 outputs on 88% of trials. The report follows the contents of the [[j-space]] at the time of reporting.

terms.term: "Think of a sport. Answer in one word."
terms.definition: The report prompt of the worked example: the model is told to pick an item from a named category and name it in a single word. One of fourteen such category prompts.
The chat-role labels of the prompt as displayed in the widget. The lens is read at the highlighted colon after "Assistant", the last token before the model's answer.

The orange bar list: the Jacobian lens readout of the residual stream at layer 92 on the paper's percent-of-depth scale, the final layer of the workspace range. Shows the top five tokens by lens score.
The grey bar list: the model's actual output distribution at the same position, shown so that internal lens content and imminent output can be compared directly.
The unmodified forward pass: lens readout and output logits with no intervention applied.
The intervention block: both readouts repeated after a lens-coordinate swap that removes the Soccer direction and installs the Rugby direction at every token position.
The model's spontaneously chosen answer, visible in the lens before it is spoken; the concept the swap removes.
The swap target: a different item from the same category, chosen from outside the model's top-10 likely outputs, whose lens vector is written in.
The number printed beside each token is its natural-log probability under that readout's softmax; bar length is proportional to the probability itself.
The model the example and the aggregate experiments run on, the paper's primary subject model.
The heading of the right-hand column: both aggregate panels pool the fourteen categories of the task battery.

terms.term: Lens vs output rank Spearman ρ
terms.definition: The y-axis of the top-right panel: the rank correlation between ten candidate answers' ordering under the lens readout and their ordering under the model's output logits.
The x-axis of the top-right panel: the three workspace layers at which the correlation is measured, on the percent-of-depth layer scale.
The middle band of layers in which the J-space behaves like a workspace; L92 is its final layer, which is why the example's lens readout is taken there.
The y-axis of the bottom-right panel: where a swap target sits in the model's ranked next-token distribution, on a log scale from 1 (top) to 1k+ (bottom).
The two x-positions of the bottom-right panel; each line connects one swap target's output rank in the clean pass to its rank after the swap.
The panel's inclusion criterion: swap targets must start outside the model's top-10 candidate outputs, so any rise is attributable to the swap rather than to an answer already in contention.
One category (top panel) or one swap trial (bottom panel); in the live widget, hovering a dot shows the trial's prompt and top lens tokens.

numbers.meaning: Answer categories in the task battery: beverage, bird, city, color, country, fruit, instrument, language, organ, planet, profession, river, sport, tree. Each contributes one dot per layer in the correlation panel.
Candidate answers per category over which each Spearman correlation is computed: their ordering under the lens is compared with their ordering under the output logits.
The three workspace layers of the correlation panel, on the percent-of-depth scale; L92 is the final layer of the workspace range and the layer of the example's readout.

Median Spearman correlation across the fourteen categories at L54, L75, and L92 in the widget's data. The correlation increases toward the end of the workspace as the model gets closer to producing the token.
Soccer's log-probability in the original pass: -0.32 under the L92 lens readout, -0.03 under the model's actual next-token logits. Both readouts agree before any intervention.
Rugby's log-probability after the swap: -0.23 under the lens, essentially 0 (probability near 1) under the output logits. The swapped-in concept becomes both the workspace content and the answer.

Swap targets are drawn at random from the category but must start outside the model's top-10 candidate outputs; the bottom-right panel displays only such targets, so the swap is tested on concepts the model was not about to say.
Swap trials displayed in the bottom-right panel of the live widget (roughly five per category).
Median swap-target output rank before versus after the swap, in the widget's displayed trials; in those trials no target ends worse than rank 10.
The log-scale range of the candidate-rank axis; 1k+ collapses all ranks of 1000 or worse, since a target can start anywhere in the vocabulary's tail.

The swap's calibration: the projection added along the target's lens vector has the same magnitude as the projection removed along the source's, so the intervention exchanges one concept for another rather than injecting extra signal.

The fraction of trials on which swaps along pure J-lens vectors drive the target into the model's top-5 outputs, quoted later in section 3.1 as the reference against which the J-space component's 59% is compared.
